$schema_note: The growth site — where the run's meaningful decisions happen. It is the same breadth/depth/sustain axis as the GDD §6 fork events, at a continuous grain. Decisions + rationale in SYSTEMS.md §4/§7. PROTOTYPE DIALS.

site.note: A camp panel reached at each breather. Player arrives with an Ember pool and allocates across the actions below. Costs are set so ~30-40 Embers buys 2-3 actions — you cannot buy all. The scarcity is the design.

actions.label: Drill the line
actions.effect: promote up to 20 units one tier

site.budget_note: The three TRIANGLE lanes (recruit/promote/provision) total 37 Embers — at ~33 on arrival you can take two of three, or two lanes plus a partial. Item (20) and hero (18) are the real temptations: taking one means giving up most of the triangle that turn.

slice_placement.after: wave 1 breather (replaces the gate-1 flat refill-to-120)
slice_placement.note: First real decision of the run. Currently a free refill — the single highest-leverage change to add meaningful choice.

slice_placement.embers_math: ~420 brood killed x 0.1 + 10 grant (wave 2 is bigger, so income scales)
slice_placement.note: Bigger pool before the hardest wave — the run-defining allocation. Whether the wave-2 income scaled correctly is a key tuning read.

relation_to_decision_events.note: The GDD §6 fork/sacrifice events are the DRAMATIC one-shot version of this same triangle. 'Free the pens vs. raid the armory' is breadth-vs-depth authored as a story beat. The growth site is the continuous, player-driven version. Same axis, two grains — the economy and the decisions pillar are one system.
relation_to_decision_events.slice_scope: The slice's 2 authored decision events (RTS-VERTICAL-SLICE §5) sit ON TOP of these growth sites, not instead of them.
